title: 3659. Partition Array Into K-Distinct Groups

examples.explanation: One possible partition is to have 2 groups: Group 1: [1, 2] Group 2: [3, 4] Each group contains k = 2 distinct elements, and all elements are used exactly once.
One possible partition is to have 2 groups: Group 1: [2, 3] Group 2: [2, 5] Each group contains k = 2 distinct elements, and all elements are used exactly once.
We cannot form groups of k = 3 distinct elements using all values exactly once.

hints: Think about how many groups of size k you need to form.
Each group must contain exactly k distinct elements.
If any element appears more times than the number of groups groups, it cannot be placed uniquely in each group.
Use a frequency map freq to count the occurrences of each element.
If the total number of elements n is not divisible by k, partitioning is impossible.
